r-m1-001.q: What is the core goal of the field of Computer Vision?
r-m1-001.correct: To enable machines to "see" and understand the visual world the way humans do
wrong: To optimize the transmission speed of large image files over the Internet
To automate video compression without decoding the data
To design specialized hardware for storing independent pixel matrices

r-m1-002.q: In the 8-bit digital image representation, what does the pixel value of a grayscale image mean?
r-m1-002.correct: It represents light intensity, ranging from 0 (completely black) to 255 (completely white)
wrong: It represents light wavelength, ranging from 0 (infrared) to 255 (ultraviolet)
It denotes the display's refresh rate, ranging from 0 Hz to 255 Hz
It specifies the 2D spatial coordinates of the pixel in the data matrix

r-m1-003.q: In the RGB color space, which color does a pixel with the value [255, 255, 0] display?
wrong: Magenta
Cyan
White

r-m1-004.q: What is the fundamental difference between how a computer and the human eye perceive an image?
r-m1-004.correct: A computer sees an image as a matrix structure of numbers representing light intensity
wrong: A computer naturally interprets the story and emotional context better than the human eye
A computer can only receive monochromatic light and cannot process color channels
A computer decodes images directly through sound waves from environmental sensors

r-m1-005.q: In the OpenCV library for Python, which function is used to display an image in a GUI window?
wrong: cv2.imread()
cv2.imwrite()
cv2.display()

r-m1-006.q: In homogeneous coordinates, a 2D point is represented as a vector (x, y, w). What does w = 0 represent?
wrong: The coordinate origin (0, 0)
The center point of the image matrix
An undefined point caused by an overflow error

r-m1-007.q: Which of the following is a core characteristic of a geometric transformation?
r-m1-007.correct: It changes the spatial structure of the image without changing the pixel values
wrong: It changes the light intensity and color of pixels while keeping the spatial coordinates unchanged
It converts the image into a binary matrix to reduce storage size
It automatically removes all chromatic aberration of the optical lens system

r-m1-008.q: Which geometric property of objects in an image does an Affine transformation always preserve?
wrong: The right angles between intersecting lines
The absolute Euclidean distance between any two points
The area ratios of complex shapes

r-m1-009.q: Which property of lines in an image does a Projective transformation preserve?
wrong: The parallelism of lines
The angles between intersecting lines
The area and perimeter of objects

r-m1-010.q: How are the Degrees of Freedom (DoF) of a geometric transformation defined?
r-m1-010.correct: The minimum number of independent parameters required to completely specify the transformation
wrong: The maximum number of pixels that can be displaced in a single transformation step
The total number of dimensions of the homogeneous coordinate matrix plus one
The number of iterations required for the geometric transformation algorithm to converge

r-m1-011.q: What is the main difference between orthographic projection and perspective projection from 3D space to 2D?
r-m1-011.correct: Orthographic projection ignores the depth effect by dropping the z axis without any division
wrong: Orthographic projection preserves the property that distant objects appear smaller than near objects
Orthographic projection requires computing a virtual vanishing point on the image plane
Orthographic projection can only be applied to cameras with ultra-wide-angle lenses

r-m1-012.q: In OpenCV, which function is used to compute a 2D rotation matrix about a center with a specified angle and scale?
wrong: cv2.warpAffine()
cv2.findHomography()
cv2.rotateMatrix()

r-m1-013.q: According to Lambert's Cosine Law, what does the intensity of diffusely reflected light from a rough surface depend on?
r-m1-013.correct: The angle between the incident light ray and the surface normal vector
wrong: The distance between the observer's eye and the camera sensor
The ratio of the refractive index of the lens glass to white light
The aperture opening and the exposure time of the camera shutter

r-m1-014.q: Which lighting components does the Phong shading model combine to simulate complete illumination?
r-m1-014.correct: Ambient light + Diffuse reflection + Specular reflection
wrong: Diffuse reflection + Light refraction + Rayleigh scattering
Ambient light + Thermal radiation (Radiosity) + Aberration scattering
Specular reflection + Lens refractive index + Ray tracing

r-m1-015.q: Which types of surface light interaction are Ray Tracing and Radiosity best suited for?
r-m1-015.correct: Ray tracing is suited to mirror-like/strongly reflective surfaces, while Radiosity is used for rough (diffuse) surfaces
wrong: Ray tracing is suited only to rough surfaces, while Radiosity is used only for convex spherical mirrors
Both techniques apply only to perfectly transparent liquid surfaces
Ray tracing is used for area light sources, while Radiosity is used for point light sources

r-m1-016.q: What physical cause underlies chromatic aberration in an optical system?
r-m1-016.correct: The refractive index of glass varies slightly with different light wavelengths
wrong: The intensity of a point light source is non-uniform when passing through the lens aperture
Charge overflow between neighboring sensor cells on the sensor array
The camera shutter opening and closing too quickly, distorting the exposure time

r-m1-017.q: Which important property of the Bidirectional Reflectance Distribution Function (BRDF) is stated in the course material?
wrong: The BRDF is always a constant for every light wavelength
The BRDF depends only on the viewing angle and not on the incident angle
The BRDF can only be applied to infinite area light sources

r-m1-018.q: Compared with a CCD sensor, what distinctive advantage does a CMOS sensor have in its signal readout mechanism?
r-m1-018.correct: It can read data from each individual pixel independently
wrong: It has higher light sensitivity and is completely unaffected by thermal noise
It never suffers from blooming under any lighting condition
It consumes more power, which speeds up ADC signal conversion

r-m1-019.q: Blooming is a limitation most commonly encountered in which type of sensor?
wrong: CMOS sensor
Infrared thermal sensor
CFA (color filter array) sensor

r-m1-020.q: In the HSV color space, which color corresponds to a Hue value of 120 degrees?
wrong: Red
Blue
Yellow

r-m1-021.q: In the YCbCr color space, widely used for JPEG image and video compression, what does the Y channel represent?
wrong: The blue chroma channel (Blue Chroma)
The red chroma channel (Red Chroma)
The color saturation channel (Saturation)

r-m1-022.q: Which metric is most commonly used to evaluate the quality of an image after compression?
wrong: BRDF (Bidirectional Reflectance Distribution Function)
DoF (Degrees of Freedom)
AGC (Automatic Gain Control)

r-m1-023.q: Which property of human vision does the JPEG compression algorithm exploit when subsampling the color channels?
r-m1-023.correct: The human eye is less sensitive to changes in color than to spatial detail
wrong: The human eye perceives only the green and red portions of the light spectrum
The human eye is more sensitive to the Chroma channel than to the Luma channel in low light
The human eye automatically white-balances every type of monochromatic light

r-m1-024.q: Which of the following groups of image file formats consists entirely of lossless compression formats?
wrong: JPEG, MP4, lossy WebP
MPEG, H.264, JPEG
AVI, WMV, FLV

r-m2-001.q: Which of the following is a basic characteristic of point operators in image processing?
r-m2-001.correct: The output pixel value at each position depends only on the input pixel value at that same position
wrong: The output pixel value is computed from a linear combination of pixels in the neighborhood
The algorithm must sort the entire pixel matrix before performing the computation
The operation can only be applied to three-channel RGB color images and cannot process grayscale images
